correctness.rationale: The full m-dimensional Fourier covariance spectrum is derived from unsigned spoke/rim vectors. Its log determinant is strictly concave with opposite endpoint derivative signs; its unique maximizer equalizes exact orbit Mahalanobis contacts. The weighted vertex sum is dimension m, so all contacts equal m. Averaging containment over this positive design and using trace-determinant AGM certifies the candidate as globally smallest enclosing ellipsoid with unique center and shape. Uniform exponential convergence of periodic analytic Fourier sums leads rigorously to a_m=1/3+5/(3m)+O(m^-2). The standard-library checker independently reconstructs covariance and small-m contacts; finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The ordinary wheel edge polytope is a canonical sparse graph-edge body. Its minimum-volume Euclidean enclosing ellipsoid gives a natural, global metric descriptor, not a narrow arbitrary parameter slice. Exact spectral shape and all-contact characterization for every order show how the two edge orbit types are balanced by optimal design, while a nontrivial \(1/m\) correction explains the unexpected one-third asymptotic contact mass despite half the vertices lying in each orbit. This is distinct from known unsigned-wheel inradius and signed-wheel Löwner geometry.
